Plan the week in one page

A subtitle nearly as big

Third level

Fourth level

A short guide to setting out the week so that each day has one clear job. It keeps the list short, puts the hard task first, and leaves a little room at the end of each day for whatever turned up. Most people find it easier to start than a long list, because the first step is always obvious, and the rest follows. Write the three things that matter, then block the time for them before anything else goes in. When something new arrives, ask which of the three it replaces. If the answer is none, it waits until next week, and that is fine, and nobody minds.

One line per day, one job per line, and a short note on what done looks like. Keep it where you will see it every morning, and cross things out by hand at the end of the day, so the page shows what moved and what did not, which is the whole point of keeping it in one place.
